To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

etidronate, clodronate and phosphonoformate ameliorate the inflammatory and necrosis side effects of zoeldronate in mice, and that the mechanisms of these effects are different for etidronate/clodronate and for phosphonoformate.
etidronate, clodronate and phosphonoformate reduce the inflammation/necrosis induced in mice by zoledronate and by non-N-BPs.

(i) pyrophosphate and non-N-BPs can enter soft-tissue-cells via phosphonoformicate-inhibitable phosphate transporters, and (ii) the side effects of the N-BP, zoledronate can be inhibited by etidronates and clodronates via inhibition of phosphonoformicate inhibitable phosphate transporters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms underlying the anti-inflammatory/necrotogenic effects of etidronate, clodronate and phosphonoformate in a mouse model.
the mechanisms by which etidronate, clodronate and other non-N-BPs ameliorate the inflammatory/necrosis-inducing side effects of zoeldronate.
the mechanisms underlying the protective effects of non-N- and N-BPs against the side effects of N-BP.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the side effects of N-BP zoeldronate are reduced by etidornate and cloodronate because these drugs are able to inhibit the phosphonoformate-sensitive phosphate transporter.

the non-N-BP etidronate, the non-N-BPs clodronate and tiludronate, the phosphate transport inhibitor phosphonoformate and the bisphosphonates zoledronate and risedronate are all capable of inhibiting the inflammatory and necrotoxic effects of the non-N-BPS etidronate in the mouse ear-pinnas model.
the N-BPs, such as zoledronate and alendronate, have a higher anti-bone-resorption efficacy than the non-N-BPs and, therefore, are more effective for the treatment of enhanced bone-resorption.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the non-N-BP clodronate is the most effective inhibitor of the side effects of the N-BP, zoledronate.

the anti-bone-resorption effects of zoledronic acid are mediated by its inhibition of farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase (FPPS) and the side effects of this drug are mediated by its transport into the cell by phosphate transporter.
etidronate, clodronate and phosphonoformate are inhibitors of phosphate transporters and that they protect against the inflammatory and necrosis effects of zoledroate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
etidronate, clodronate and phosphonoformate are inhibitors of phosphate transporters and that etidronates and clodronates may be used as inhibitors of phosphate transport in soft tissues.
the non-N-BPs etidronate, clodronate and phosphonoformate reduce the inflammatory and necroic side effects of N-BP zoeldronate in mice, but only etidronate is currently used in humans.

etidronate, clodronate and phosphonoformate inhibit phosphate-transporters that mediate the entry of zoledronat and of inflammatory/necrotogenic non-N-BPs in soft tissues, and this inhibition ameliorates the side effects of the N-BP, zoledronate.
